one_line_contribution: Define per-item responsibility for a failed agent episode by seed-replicated removal re-runs (12 seeds, two 6-seed blocks, plus an emptied-set arm), then measure (a) how far cheap attributions - self-report, teacher-forced confidence gain, position prior, single-seed leave-one-out - fall below a fresh 6-seed intervention replicate scored on the same episodes, (b) how often no single item is responsible at all, and (c) whether duplicating a culprit converts single into joint responsibility.
closest_prior_work: arXiv:2608.20627, 'When Failures Propagate: Causal Failure Attribution in Agentic RAG' (AgenticRAG-FP), 2026-08-20, verified with the literature command (HF channel; s2cli paper 2608.20627 returned it). It is an interventional failure-attribution benchmark that injects a certified fault at a specified hop, re-executes the downstream trajectory, and scores post-hoc diagnosers against the known ground-truth fault - the same contribution shape as this proposal's E2 planted-culprit arm plus E3 method scoring, and it appears on the proposal's own novelty card while being absent from its Preprint Collision Check. It does not sink the proposal: its unit is a retrieval hop fault in multi-hop RAG, it has no seed replication (which is precisely this proposal's live axis, since ALFWorld outcomes are stochastic and a single re-run is a coin flip), no attributability rate over natural failures, and no joint-responsibility/duplication arm. Second threat: CUE-R arXiv:2604.05467 (verified, S2, 2 citations) already defines per-evidence-item utility by REMOVE/REPLACE/DUPLICATE interventions - the proposal's exact operator set - so the delta is 'same operators, multi-step stochastic agent, failure episodes', which reviewers will read as a setting transfer. Third: arXiv:2507.04480 'Source Attribution in Retrieval-Augmented Generation' (PKDD/ECML Workshops 2025, 7 citations; direct `s2cli paper 2507.04480` returned 'not found', verified instead by title search on S2) already quantifies how well SHAP approximations mirror exact document attributions while minimizing costly LLM interactions - i.e. the accuracy-versus-cost frontier, one setting removed. Fourth, for the headline prediction specifically: arXiv:2605.29463 'Honest Lying: Understanding Memory Confabulation in Reflexive Agents' (from the novelty card) already shows on ALFWorld that agents confidently mis-diagnose their own failures and act on the mis-diagnosis, which substantially deflates P1 ('self-report is a bad attributor') as a headline finding.
strongest_objection: The ceiling is selected on the same estimand it is supposed to bound, so the central gaps are partly manufactured. The scoring pool is defined as the episodes where the 12-seed one-sided 95% lower bound on max_i r_i clears zero - i.e. episodes pre-selected for a large, LOO-detectable removal effect (at m=12 this needs r_i of about 0.33, and the design's own power table implies the retained culprits mostly carry r of 0.5-0.7). The ceiling C is then a fresh 6-seed run of that same removal estimator. Disjoint seeds remove seed-level correlation but not the selection on the estimand: any removal-based estimator inherits a large true signal on this pool by construction, while self-report, confidence gain and position prior do not. P1, P2, P6 and P7 are all gaps against that one selected C (the entailment check flags the shared term), so the 20-25 point margins can be met without any of the cheap methods being bad in an unselected population - a reviewer will say the benchmark measures its own selection rule. The second half of the objection is P4, the claim that 'most memory-caused natural failures are not attributable to any single item': at 12 seeds the rule is blind to any true r below about 0.33, so a high non-attributability rate is largely a statement about the rule's power, not about the world, and it is the finding the abstract leads with. Releasing the r_i distribution mitigates but does not license the headline sentence.
what_would_fix_it: (1) Score the methods on an unselected pool as the primary analysis - every memory-caused failure, with a continuous criterion (rank correlation of each method's scores against the 12-seed r_i vector, or top-1 accuracy restricted to episodes where the label is well-determined by a criterion that is not the removal statistic itself) - and report the attributable-pool top-1 accuracies as the secondary, selection-inflated view; the planted-only oracle set, which is unselected, should carry P1-P3 by design rather than only as a fallback under the C-PP gate. (2) Restate P4 as a power-explicit statement ('fewer than X% have a single item with r >= 0.33') or, better, report the full distribution of max_i r_i with intervals as the headline instead of a thresholded rate. (3) Add the external LLM-diagnoser baseline (below); without it the method set contains no method the failure-attribution literature actually uses. (4) Fix the three predictions the entailment check flags: make the random tie-break the primary scoring of the m=1 point and pre-register P3a's falsifier as a fraction of the analytic single-seed ceiling implied by the E0 p(S); make P6's primary estimand the label-transfer rate on the subset where reader 2 also fails at base, with the base-rate mismatch reported separately, or the arm measures backbone base rates rather than transfer of attribution; replace P5b's significance count with a pooled interaction magnitude and CI, since a 12%-versus-10% margin is far inside the cluster-bootstrap width at 6 seeds per subset. (5) Cite and position against arXiv:2608.20627 and arXiv:2605.29463 explicitly - a benchmark paper whose collision check omits the nearest interventional attribution benchmark will be read as not having looked.
missing_baseline: An external LLM diagnoser: a second call that sees the full failed trajectory plus the k retrieved items and names the responsible item (or 'none'). That is the method every prior failure-attribution paper evaluates (A2P arXiv:2509.10401, CausalFlow arXiv:2605.25338, the Who&When-style root-cause benchmarks, and the diagnosers scored in AgenticRAG-FP arXiv:2608.20627), and it is strictly stronger than the acting agent's own post-episode self-report, which is the only judge-like method in E3. Without it the paper claims that 'the cheap attributions current systems rely on' fail while omitting the cheap attribution the attribution literature actually relies on, and the self-report result is confounded with self-knowledge rather than diagnosability. A second, cheaper omission: an offline reuse estimator that scores items from episodes already in the k-sweep and nested-k logs (item present versus absent across games, with matching), which costs zero new episodes and is the natural 'do I need fresh re-runs at all' floor on the accuracy-versus-cost frontier the paper's headline figure claims to chart.
preprint_collision: No verified collision on the full claim, but the proposal's own check is incomplete in a way that matters for a benchmark paper. Channels: every query below was answered by the literature command (s2cli, S2 + HF, both ok); WebSearch was unavailable in this session and was not used. Queries run: (1) --recent, 'attribute agent failure to individual retrieved memory item intervention re-run counterfactual ground truth benchmark' -> arXiv:2608.20627 (AgenticRAG-FP, top hit), 2607.10608, 2607.13083, 2608.00017, 2509.10401, 2509.08682, 2602.16313 - nothing at item level with seed replication. (2) all-time, 'leave-one-out counterfactual removal of retrieved item stochastic policy seed replication noisy utility responsibility label' -> arXiv:2604.05467 (CUE-R), 2607.27888, 2605.25507, 2510.27484 (Thought Branches: resampling for causal analysis of reasoning - the same 'one run is not a counterfactual' argument, at the CoT-step level), 1909.10447 - no item-level agent-memory hit. (3) closest named method, 'CUE-R intervention based per evidence item utility remove replace duplicate RAG' -> arXiv:2604.05467 confirmed plus 2608.23252, 2605.01302 - all single-shot RAG. (4) home vocabulary, 'Shapley value data valuation stochastic noisy utility sample complexity ranking stability' -> Data Shapley 1904.02868, SVARM 2302.00736, shapiq 2410.01649 - the sample-cost-of-a-noisy-utility question is well developed there and the proposal does not engage it. (5) 'source attribution RAG Shapley contribution of each source document' -> arXiv:2507.04480 verified (S2, PKDD/ECML Workshops, 2025-07-06, 7 citations), matching the proposal's description. (6) --recent, 'does the model know which retrieved example it used self-report faithfulness counterfactual' -> 2602.02639, 2502.18156, 2601.10700 - classification/reasoning only, so the proposal's claim that self-report has never been tested against re-runs for retrieved items holds. IDs verified by direct lookup: 2604.05467, 2605.25338 (CausalFlow, 8 citations, step-level as described), 2607.10608, 2511.20857, 2602.16313, 2608.20627. Verified incidentally in search returns: 2509.10401, 2509.08682, 2607.13083, 2602.02639, 2502.18156. Verified by title search after a failed id lookup: 2507.04480. Not verified by me: 2507.05257, 2605.18565, 2604.20006, 2604.17658, 2509.23735, 2401.07927, 2307.08678, 2311.07466, and every id cited from the brief (2605.08374, 2608.02508, 2607.22562, 2607.21106, 2606.17628, 2603.04549). Judgement on the check itself: it is unusually specific and its three query classes are the right ones, and its negative conclusion survives my searches on the item-level-plus-seed-replication combination. But it names five papers under the mechanism query and omits arXiv:2608.20627, the single nearest interventional failure-attribution benchmark, which the proposal's own automated novelty card returned at sim 0.50 - the strongest evidence that the check was run before, and not reconciled with, the card. It also omits arXiv:2605.29463 (Honest Lying, ALFWorld self-diagnosis confabulation), which is directly on the headline P1 claim. Both omissions are the kind an area chair reads as a novelty argument that has not been closed.
